channel_videos.description:
本日の日本市況概説






日本の日経平均株価は4月8日に5.3％上昇しました。米国とイランによる2週間の停戦合意を受けて原油価格が下落し、安心感からリリーフラリーが発生したことが背景です。 






しかし、実質家計消費支出が前年比1.8％減と弱く、国内の基調は依然として脆弱なままでした。






注目銘柄はゼンショーです。創業者の小川賢太郎氏の死去を受けて、後継体制（サクセッション）への関心が高まっています。

[Yukkuri Explainer] Can Politics Update in Real Time? Team Mirai and Digital Democracy
channel_videos_en.description:
[Short Video]
https://youtube.com/shorts/vh6EVfHahGU?feature=share

[Note Article]
https://note.com/ryosao/n/nda6f5880fef8?hl=en

What if politics could update in real time, like a weather app?

In this video, I explain digital democracy in a simple way through the cases of Taiwan and Team Mirai in Japan.

Digital democracy is a new way of thinking about politics. Instead of relying only on elections held once every few years, it aims to gather citizens' opinions continuously and reflect them in policy through digital technology.

This video covers:
- what digital democracy means
- how Taiwan used online civic discussion in real policy-making
- how tools such as Polis helped find common ground
- why Audrey Tang became a key figure in this field
- how Team Mirai in Japan is trying to apply similar ideas
- how AI can support discussion without replacing human decision-making
- ideas such as futarchy, quadratic voting, and quadratic funding

Today, many democracies face polarization, distrust, and the limits of old political systems.
Digital democracy may offer one possible way to update how politics works in the age of the internet and AI.

This video is for informational and educational purposes only and does not support any specific political position.

#Politics
#Japan
#Taiwan
#TeamMirai
#AI
#Yukkuri

channel_videos_en.title: [Yukkuri Explainer] Can Politics Update in Real Time? Team Mirai and Digital Democracy
channel_videos_en.description:
[Full Video]
https://youtu.be/ESrAk9zqLvw

[Note Article]
https://note.com/ryosao/n/nda6f5880fef8?hl=en

In this video, I explain digital democracy, one of the key ideas associated with Team Mirai, which drew attention in Japan’s recent election.

Digital democracy is a system that gathers citizens’ opinions in real time and reflects them in politics.

Instead of relying only on elections held every few years, it is attracting attention as a new form of democracy that allows people to participate in politics on a more continuous basis.

In Taiwan, systems that turn online public discussion into actual policy have already been put into practice, and similar efforts are now beginning in Japan.

For a deeper explanation, please watch the full video.
